title: Langfuse instrumentation lab
description: Create a trace with nested work and inspect it without sending private content.
objectives: Instrument one request with parent and child observations
Inspect timing, errors, and data captured by telemetry
explanation: A trace connects work belonging to one request. Start with a request observation and nest retrieval, model generation, or tool observations beneath it. Use names and version metadata that make comparisons meaningful. Timing without a request relationship makes multi-step failures harder to diagnose.

The example uses the documented Langfuse Python get_client and start_as_current_observation interfaces. Install a compatible SDK in an isolated environment and configure your own project keys and base URL through environment variables. Run only invented data first, then inspect which attributes reached the project.

Close observations on both success and failure, and flush short-lived scripts so buffered events can be delivered. Redact or omit sensitive content before export. A tracing outage should not silently corrupt the application result; decide whether to drop telemetry, buffer it, or alert within bounded limits.

terms.definition: A connected record of work for one request.
An instrumented operation within a trace.
Sending buffered telemetry before a process exits.

example: langfuse_trace.py records a synthetic request and a child lookup returning only a count. It does not call a model. Inspect that the lookup appears under the request and that no secret key or private document is included.
mistakes: Placing tracing secret keys in front-end code.
Assuming a trace proves the answer is correct.
Allowing telemetry queues to grow without limits.
exercise: Configure a test Langfuse project with your own environment variables and run the optional sample. Find the parent-child relationship, timestamps, and synthetic output count. Add a deliberate local error and inspect how it is recorded.

code.title: Trace a synthetic lookup
code.note: Optional integration example. Requires a compatible langfuse SDK and your own LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL. Sends synthetic telemetry; not run by the offline checks.

questions.question: What connects retrieval and generation observations in one request?
questions.answer: Their shared trace and parent-child relationships.
questions.distractor: Identical timestamps are the only possible link.

questions.question: Why flush a short-lived tracing script?
questions.answer: Buffered telemetry might otherwise remain unsent when the process exits.

questions.question: A trace contains a full private document. What should change?
questions.answer: Redact or omit sensitive payloads before export and review retention and access.
questions.distractor: Make the tracing project public to ease debugging.

questions.question: Does successful trace delivery establish answer quality?
questions.answer: No. Tracing records execution; evaluation measures the required behavior.
questions.distractor: Yes, every recorded output is correct.

questions.question: Where do Langfuse secret keys belong?
questions.answer: In the server or local process environment with appropriate access controls.
questions.distractor: In a public browser JavaScript bundle.
